MOD=Kun|S=je|O=de naam van de toepassing|A=nog eens|I=zeggen?
Can you say the application's name again?
A colleague has mentioned an application whose name you missed. Ask them informally to say the name again.
Nog eens asks for the same name again, not for another application.
Could you please repeat the last step?
During formal guidance, you miss the final instruction. Ask the person politely to repeat that last step.
Formal u keeps kunt in inversion. De laatste stap is one particular step, not the whole procedure.
I did not catch the start of your question.
A customer has just asked you something over the phone. Address them formally and explain that you did not catch the beginning.
Heb ... verstaan is a perfect, not a possession construction. Verstaan concerns hearing the spoken wording clearly.
Which number did you just mention?
A customer has read a number, but you are not sure which one you heard. Ask them formally to repeat the number they just mentioned.
Zojuist identifies the immediately preceding speech. Formal hebt u is valid; heeft u is also standard.
Could you say the instruction a little more slowly?
A colleague is explaining a step too quickly for you to follow. Politely ask them informally to say the instruction more slowly.
Zou je softens the request. Iets langzamer asks for a modest change in pace, not different content.
The last word keeps cutting out.
During a remote conversation, you repeatedly miss the final word because the sound drops out. Describe this repeated symptom to your colleague.
Steeds indicates recurrence. Valt ... weg is separable and does not mean that the spoken word is wrong.
Can you say the abbreviation letter by letter?
A colleague uses an unfamiliar abbreviation. Ask them informally to give its letters separately so you can write it down.
Letter voor letter specifies the way of saying the abbreviation, not an expansion of its meaning.
Did you say Monday or Tuesday?
A customer has just given a date, but you are unsure which weekday you heard. Ask formally whether they said Monday or Tuesday.
Zei checks what was said in the completed exchange. Of presents two possible days rather than confirming either one.
I will repeat the digits one at a time.
A colleague did not catch a reference number you gave. Promise to repeat its digits one at a time.
This is a commitment to repeat, not a request that the colleague repeat. Één voor één means individually.
S=Ik|V=schrijf|O=de instructie|PART=op|TE=om ze correct te kunnen herhalen.
I am writing down the instruction so I can repeat it correctly.
A colleague asks why you are taking notes during an explanation. Say that you are writing the instruction down so you can repeat it accurately.
Opschrijven splits as schrijf ... op. Ze refers to de instructie; om te kunnen herhalen gives the purpose.
What do you mean by an active account?
A colleague refers to an active account while discussing a request. Ask informally what they mean by that description.
Bedoelen met asks about the speaker's intended meaning. An active account is not automatically an account with every permission.
What does this message mean on this screen?
You are learning an interface and see a message you do not understand. Ask a colleague what the message means there.
De melding is a de-word and takes deze. Asking its meaning does not assert that it is an error or disruption.
V=Bedoelt|S=u|G=dat het account pas is aangemaakt?
Do you mean that the account was created recently?
A customer describes an account as new. Ask formally whether they mean it was created recently rather than merely being unfamiliar to them.
Pas identifies recent creation. The dat-clause contains a passive/result perfect; the customer is not necessarily the person who created it.
MOD=Kun|S=je|O=het verschil tussen een melding en een foutmelding|I=uitleggen?
Can you explain the difference between a report and an error message?
You are learning support terminology. Ask a colleague informally to explain how a general report differs from an error message.
Tussen ... en links the compared terms. A user report is not necessarily a system-generated error message.
I do not know what this abbreviation stands for.
A colleague uses an abbreviation without explaining it. Tell them that you do not know what its letters stand for.
Waar ... voor stands for the prepositional reference in this embedded question; staat is final.
S=Een tijdelijke oplossing|V=is|NEG=niet altijd|C=een definitieve oplossing.
A workaround is not always a permanent solution.
A colleague assumes that a temporary workaround has permanently fixed an issue. Explain that those two outcomes are not always the same.
Niet altijd leaves open that some temporary solutions may become permanent. It does not claim that every workaround is useless.
Could you describe the problem in other words?
A customer's description contains wording you cannot interpret. Address them formally and ask for the same problem to be described differently.
In andere woorden changes the wording, not the underlying problem or the facts being reported.
V=Bedoel|S=je|O=technische toegang|C=of toestemming van de eigenaar?
Do you mean technical access or the owner's permission?
A colleague says access is needed, but the requirement is ambiguous. Ask whether they mean the technical capability or the owner's authorisation.
Of offers two different requirements. Being technically able to open something does not by itself imply permission.
I understood the term new as unfamiliar.
You realise you may have misunderstood a colleague's description of an account. Explain that you interpreted new as unfamiliar.
This reports your interpretation, not a definition equating nieuw and onbekend. The distinction is exactly what needs clarifying.
G=Als je afsluiten zegt,|V=bedoel|S=je|G=dan dat het ticket bewaard blijft?
When you say close, do you mean the ticket will be kept?
A colleague tells you to close a ticket. Check informally that closing it will preserve the record rather than delete it.
The first clause quotes the action being discussed. Bewaard blijft describes retention; the question does not instruct deletion.
Can you demonstrate which steps you normally follow?
You are learning a colleague's normal procedure for a task. Ask informally to see the steps demonstrated in their usual order.
Normaal identifies the regular procedure, not necessarily a newly invented workaround. Volgt is final inside the embedded clause.
Could you demonstrate the first action a little more slowly?
A trainer demonstrates a process too quickly. Address them formally and ask for the first action to be shown more slowly.
The request concerns the first action only. Wat softens the requested change of pace.
Where do you click to open the user details?
A colleague is demonstrating a support application. Ask informally which location they click to open the user details.
Klik before subject je has no -t. Om te openen gives the purpose of the click; it does not ask to share confidential user details.
I am now trying to carry out the same step myself.
After watching a colleague demonstrate a step, explain that you are now attempting that same step independently.
Proberen takes a te-infinitive. Uitvoeren is separable, so te stands between uit and voeren; an attempt is not yet success.
S=Ik|V=ben|O=de volgorde van de handelingen|F=aan het|I=noteren.
I am writing down the sequence of the actions.
During a demonstration, a colleague asks why you have paused. Explain that you are currently writing down the action sequence.
Aan het noteren describes the current activity. De volgorde is singular even though handelingen is plural.
Are we using only test data for this exercise?
Before following a demonstration, check with your colleague that the exercise uses test data only.
Uitsluitend means exclusively. This asks what data will be used; it is not permission to use real user data.
I followed the demonstrated steps in the same order.
A colleague asks whether your attempt matched the demonstration. Report that you followed its steps in the same order.
Heb gevolgd reports a completed attempt. It does not add a claim that the result was successful.
T=Bij de tweede stap|PAST=zag|S=ik|O=een ander venster dan in jouw voorbeeld.
At the second step I saw a different window from the one in your example.
Your completed attempt differed from a colleague's demonstration. Explain that a different window appeared to you at the second step.
Zag reports your observation, not its cause. Dan compares the observed window with the colleague's example.
Can you point out the component you mean?
A colleague refers to a component during a demonstration, but you cannot identify it. Ask informally for them to point it out.
Dat je bedoelt is a relative clause modifying het onderdeel; dat is not a demonstrative object here.
Let's split the explanation into three short steps.
An explanation has become hard to follow. Suggest breaking it into three short stages before continuing.
Opsplitsen remains joined after laten. Drie korte stappen specifies the proposed structure without claiming it is the only valid procedure.
Q=Over welke versie van de toepassing|V=hebben|S=we|O=het?
Which version of the application are we talking about?
A colleague discusses application behaviour without naming the version. Ask which version the conversation concerns.
Het hebben over is a fixed expression for discussing something; over is fronted with the question phrase.
Which part of the instruction should I carry out first?
You have received several instructions without a clear starting point. Ask a colleague which part you should do first.
The question asks about the first required action. It does not weaken an obligation into a mere preference.
S=Ik|V=heb|NEG=nog geen|O=concreet voorbeeld van het gewenste resultaat.
I do not yet have a concrete example of the desired result.
You are asked to configure something but cannot picture the target outcome. Explain that you still lack a concrete example of it.
Nog geen negates an indefinite example. Een concreet voorbeeld would have no -e with singular het voorbeeld.
MOD=Kunt|S=u|I=aangeven|G=welke gebruiker de melding heeft gemaakt?
Could you indicate which user submitted the report?
A customer's report does not identify the person who submitted it. Ask formally which user created the report.
Welke gebruiker is the embedded subject. Heeft gemaakt reports submission, not whether that user caused the problem.
V=Gaat|S=het|PP=om één werkplek|C=of om het hele team?
Does this concern one workstation or the entire team?
A colleague gives a vague description of an issue's scope. Ask whether one workstation or the whole team is involved.
Gaat het om is a yes/no-style concern question, not a question-word phrase. Eén contrasts one workstation with the larger team.
S=Ik|V=heb|O=de volledige beschrijving|C=nodig|TE=om uw vraag goed te begrijpen.
I need the full description to understand your question properly.
A customer provides only part of a request. Address them formally and explain why you need the complete description.
Heb nodig expresses need; om te begrijpen gives its purpose. This does not request passwords or secret codes.
Can you clarify which step we may skip?
A colleague says that part of a procedure may be omitted but does not identify it. Ask informally which step may be skipped.
Mogen in the embedded clause concerns permission. It does not say that the step is technically impossible.
S=Ik|V=weet|NEG=niet|G=of je de nieuwe of de bestaande omgeving bedoelt.
I do not know whether you mean the new or the existing environment.
A colleague refers to an environment while two are under discussion. Explain informally that you cannot tell whether they mean the new or existing one.
The first of means whether; the second of separates the two possible environments. New and existing refer to status, not familiarity.
I have put my additional questions below the description.
A teammate asks where to find your requests for clarification. Say that you added those questions below the description.
Gezet is the participle of zetten. Onder gives a document position rather than ownership of the questions.
PP=Zonder een duidelijke omschrijving|V=kan|S=ik|NEG=niet|I=beoordelen|G=wat er moet gebeuren.
Without a clear description, I cannot judge what needs to happen.
A colleague asks you to act on an unclear request. Explain that you need a clear description before judging the required action.
The fronted prerequisite is one constituent; kan precedes ik. Wat er moet gebeuren is the content of the judgement.
Ik kan zonder een duidelijke omschrijving niet beoordelen wat er moet gebeuren.
Without a clear description, I cannot judge what needs to happen.
The subject is first instead of the prerequisite phrase; the missing information and inability to judge remain unchanged.
V=Begrijp|S=ik|C=goed|G=dat we eerst toestemming moeten vragen?
Do I understand correctly that we must ask permission first?
A colleague explains a change procedure. Check informally that asking for permission must happen before the other work.
Moeten expresses obligation. Eerst establishes the required order; the question does not itself grant permission.
V=Bedoel|S=je|G=dat het probleem bij elke aanmelding optreedt?
Do you mean the problem occurs every time someone signs in?
A colleague describes repeated sign-in trouble. Check informally whether the problem happens on every sign-in attempt rather than only occasionally.
Bij elke aanmelding means every time, not sometimes. Optreedt stays joined at the end of the embedded clause.
I will briefly summarise your question.
A customer has given a lengthy explanation. Address them formally and announce that you will briefly summarise their question.
Uw is formal possessive. Vat ... samen is separable; this announces a summary without claiming to have resolved the request.
V=Klopt|S=het|G=dat de huidige gegevens bewaard moeten blijven?
Is it correct that the existing data must be kept?
Before following a change instruction, check with a colleague that the existing data must remain intact.
Klopt het dat checks a proposition. Bewaard moeten blijven preserves the obligation to keep the data, not merely a preference.
MOD=Kun|S=je|I=bevestigen|G=dat ik het juiste bestand heb geopend?
Can you confirm that I opened the correct file?
You selected a file while following a colleague's directions. Ask informally for confirmation that it is the intended file.
The confirmation concerns file selection, not authorisation for all later edits. Heb geopend is a final perfect group.
I understood your answer as a confirmation.
A formally addressed colleague's answer may have been ambiguous. Explain that you interpreted it as confirmation rather than an open question.
Als een bevestiging describes your interpretation. It does not prove what the other speaker intended.
S=Een ontvangen bericht|V=is|NEG=niet automatisch|C=een begrepen bericht.
A received message is not automatically an understood message.
A colleague assumes receipt proves that everyone understood an update. Explain that receiving a message does not automatically mean understanding it.
Ontvangen and begrepen are attributive participles. Niet automatisch rejects the inference, not the possibility of understanding.
G=Voordat ik verderga,|V=wil|S=ik|O=de volgorde van de stappen|I=controleren.
Before I continue, I want to check the order of the steps.
You are following a procedure and need to confirm its sequence before continuing. Tell your colleague you want to check that sequence first.
The entire voordat-clause is first; wil comes before ik. Verderga is joined inside the subordinate clause.
MOD=Zou|S=u|I=kunnen aangeven|G=welk deel van mijn samenvatting niet klopt?
Could you indicate which part of my summary is not correct?
A customer says your summary is inaccurate. Ask formally which part does not match what they meant.
The request asks for a specific correction, not a repetition of the whole story. Niet klopt negates that part's accuracy.
Let's briefly record the agreement in the ticket.
You and a colleague have just clarified an arrangement. Suggest recording the agreement briefly in the support ticket.
Vastleggen means record/document the agreement. It does not mean close or delete the ticket.
S=Ik|V=leer|O=de Nederlandse termen voor dit werk|C=nog.
I am still learning the Dutch terms for this work.
A colleague notices that you sometimes need a word explained. Say that you are still learning the Dutch terminology for this work.
Nog indicates that learning continues. It does not imply that you lack the underlying technical knowledge.
Can you write the difficult words in the chat?
During a call, you cannot catch some technical words clearly. Ask a colleague informally to write those words in the chat.
The request changes the communication channel, not the meaning of the terms. Difficult words do not automatically mean complicated technical problems.
S=Ik|V=begrijp|NEG=niet altijd|O=de afkortingen die jullie gebruiken.
I do not always understand the abbreviations you use.
Your team often uses abbreviations without explanation. Tell your colleagues informally that you do not always understand those abbreviations.
Niet altijd does not mean never. Die jullie gebruiken is a relative clause modifying plural afkortingen.
How do you pronounce this technical term?
You have seen a technical term in writing and want to use it in conversation. Ask a colleague informally how to pronounce it.
Uitspreken splits as spreek ... uit. Je after the finite verb takes the stem without -t.
Could you describe that expression in ordinary words?
A customer uses an expression you cannot follow. Address them formally and ask for its meaning in simpler wording.
Ordinary wording should preserve the same meaning. The request does not suggest that the customer's language is incorrect.
I can hear the words, but I do not yet understand the intention.
A colleague has repeated an instruction clearly, but its purpose is still unclear to you. Explain the difference between hearing the words and understanding the intention.
Verstaan concerns the spoken wording here; begrijpen concerns meaning. Nog niet leaves open later understanding.
S=Ik|V=herhaal|O=de zin|A=hardop|TE=om de uitspraak te oefenen.
I repeat the sentence aloud to practise the pronunciation.
A colleague asks why you are saying a work phrase aloud. Explain that you are repeating it to practise its pronunciation.
Hardop means aloud. Om te oefenen describes your practice purpose, not an automatic pronunciation assessment.
S=Ik|V=onthoud|O=de term|C=beter|G=als ik er een voorbeeld bij noteer.
I remember the term better when I write down an example with it.
You are explaining your workplace-language learning method to a colleague. Say that noting an example helps you remember a term better.
Er ... bij refers to adding something alongside the term. Als describes the condition that improves retention.
S=Ik|V=voel|R=me|C=zeker genoeg om deze vraag in het Nederlands te stellen.
I feel confident enough to ask this question in Dutch.
A colleague offers to switch languages before you ask a work question. Say that you feel confident enough to ask this one in Dutch.
Me is reflexive. Genoeg om te stellen expresses sufficient confidence for this question, not mastery of all Dutch.
May I first formulate my answer in simple words?
You are asked a work question with unfamiliar terminology. Politely ask whether you may first express your answer in simple wording.
Mag asks permission for a communication approach. Eerst establishes a first attempt rather than a permanent rule against technical terms.
